q: 'Anubhav' is an online platform on which:

options.A: Serving railway employees record their daily attendance
options.B: Pension cases of railway pensioners are processed by the Accounts Office
options.C: Retiring and retired Government employees share their experiences and suggestions relating to their service
options.D: Grievances of serving railway employees are lodged and monitored

e: Anubhav is a DoP and PW online platform on which retiring and retired Government employees share their experiences, suggestions and feedback from their service career for use by the Government.

q: Where the Reporting Officer has not had an opportunity to observe the work and conduct of a railway servant for the minimum prescribed period during the report year, the correct course in regard to his Annual Performance Appraisal Report is to:

options.A: Write the report on the basis of the report of the previous year
options.B: Record a 'No Report Certificate' in the report for that year
options.C: Award a 'Good' grading to the railway servant by default
options.D: Obtain the report from the recognised trade union of the cadre

e: Under the APAR instructions in IREM, where the Reporting Officer has not observed the work and conduct of the employee for the minimum prescribed period, a No Report Certificate is recorded for that year instead of a report based on guesswork.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding probation and confirmation of a railway servant:
1. On the expiry of the period of probation, a railway servant is automatically confirmed in the post even without any specific order of confirmation.
2. A railway servant who has completed his period of probation satisfactorily is entitled to confirmation even if no permanent vacancy is available for his confirmation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Neither statement is correct: expiry of probation does not by itself confirm an employee, a specific confirmation order is required, and confirmation can be made only against a permanent vacancy, so satisfactory probation alone creates no right to confirmation.

q: For journeys performed by a railway servant under the Leave Travel Concession, the class of accommodation and the fare entitlement admissible to him are determined with reference to:

options.A: The length of his service
options.B: The class in which the members of his family prefer to travel
options.C: A flat economy-class entitlement prescribed for all railway servants
options.D: His entitlement for journeys performed on official tour

e: Under the LTC rules, the class of accommodation and fare entitlement for an LTC journey are the same as the employee's entitlement for a journey on official tour, not a flat class for all.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 60,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 30,000 per month
options.B: Rs 12,000 per month
options.C: Rs 18,000 per month
options.D: Rs 20,000 per month

e: Normal rate family pension under the RS (Pension) Rules is 30 percent of last basic pay: 30 percent of Rs 60,000 = Rs 18,000 per month.

q: After considering the report of the Inquiring Authority in a major penalty proceeding, the disciplinary authority, before passing final orders in the case, may:

options.A: Enhance the charges against the railway servant without giving him any notice
options.B: Remit the case to the Inquiring Authority for further inquiry on specified points
options.C: Direct that the case be tried afresh by a criminal court
options.D: Delegate its power of passing final orders to the Inquiring Authority

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules, after considering the inquiry report the disciplinary authority may remit the case to the Inquiring Authority for further inquiry on specified points before passing final orders.

q: A railway servant performs a journey by road between two stations which are connected by rail. The mileage allowance admissible to him for the road journey is ordinarily:

options.A: Admissible at double the fare admissible for the rail journey
options.B: Admissible at the highest road rate, without any restriction
options.C: Not admissible in any case
options.D: Restricted to the amount that would have been admissible had the journey been performed by rail, unless the journey by road is certified to be in public interest

e: For a road journey between rail-connected stations, mileage allowance is restricted to the amount admissible had the journey been performed by rail, unless the road journey is certified to be in public interest, as per the TA rules in IREM.

q: Where the leave account of a railway servant is lost, or is otherwise not available in the office, the leave account is reconstructed:

options.A: On the basis of available collateral records, such as pay bills, absentee statements and the entries in his Service Book
options.B: By crediting him with 300 days of Leave on Average Pay in all cases
options.C: Only from the date of the loss, ignoring the leave availed of by him earlier
options.D: Solely on the basis of a declaration made by the railway servant himself

e: A lost leave account is reconstructed from available collateral records such as pay bills, absentee statements and Service Book entries; it is not rebuilt merely on the employee's own declaration.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Administrative Tribunal:
1. Service matters of railway servants fall within the jurisdiction of the Central Administrative Tribunal.
2. Ordinarily, the Tribunal does not admit an application unless the applicant has exhausted the remedies available to him under the service rules applicable to him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: service matters of railway servants fall within CAT jurisdiction under the Administrative Tribunals Act, and the Tribunal ordinarily does not admit an application unless the applicant has exhausted the remedies available under the applicable service rules.

q: In a major penalty proceeding under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the charged railway servant admits all the articles of charge in his written statement of defence. In such a case, the disciplinary authority may:

options.A: Hold a full departmental inquiry in every case, regardless of the admission
options.B: Impose the penalty on the railway servant on the basis of his admission, without holding a further inquiry
options.C: Drop the proceedings automatically on account of the admission
options.D: Refer the case for trial to a criminal court

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules, where the charged employee admits all the articles of charge in his written statement of defence, the disciplinary authority may impose the penalty on the basis of the admission without holding a further inquiry.

q: A railway servant who is permanently absorbed in a public sector undertaking may, in lieu of the monthly pro-rata pension admissible to him for the qualifying service rendered by him under the Railways, opt for:

options.A: Full pension, as if he had retired on superannuation from the Railways
options.B: Family pension for the members of his family
options.C: No terminal benefit of any kind in respect of his railway service
options.D: A lump sum amount, representing the capital value of the pension, in accordance with the terms of his absorption

e: On permanent absorption in a PSU, a railway servant entitled to pro-rata monthly pension for his railway qualifying service may instead opt for a lump sum amount representing the capital value of that pension, under the absorption terms in the RS (Pension) Rules.

q:
Consider the following statements under the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. The right to obtain information under the Act is available only to a citizen of India.
2. A company or a body of persons, not being a citizen, can itself make an application under the Act in its own name.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: under Section 3 of the RTI Act the right to information is available only to citizens of India, so a company or body, not being a citizen, cannot apply in its own name, though its citizen officers may.

q: 'Induction training' imparted on the Railways is distinguished from 'refresher training' in that induction training is:

options.A: Imparted only to gazetted railway officers
options.B: Imparted to a railway servant only after he completes twenty years of service
options.C: Imparted to new entrants to familiarise them with their duties and with the organisation, whereas refresher training is imparted to serving staff to update their knowledge and skills
options.D: Imparted only to staff employed in railway workshops

e: Induction training is given to new entrants to familiarise them with their duties and the organisation, while refresher training is given to serving staff to update knowledge and skills, as per the training framework in IREM.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a fine cannot be imposed on an employed person who is:

options.A: Above the age of fifty-eight years
options.B: Under the age of fifteen years
options.C: A member of a recognised trade union
options.D: Employed on daily wages

e: Section 16 of the Payment of Wages Act, read with the prohibition on fines on young workers, bars imposition of a fine on an employed person under the age of fifteen years.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Overtime work of staff employed in a railway workshop is regulated under the Factories Act, 1948, which provides wages at twice the ordinary rate for work performed beyond the prescribed hours.
2. Overtime Allowance under the Hours of Employment Regulations is payable to such workshop staff in addition to the overtime wages under the Factories Act, 1948 for the same hours of work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: workshop staff overtime is governed by the Factories Act, 1948, which prescribes wages at twice the ordinary rate beyond the prescribed hours, and HOER Overtime Allowance is not payable in addition for the same hours.

q: In regard to the amount standing at the credit of a subscriber in the General Provident Fund, the correct position is that the amount:

options.A: Can be attached by any creditor of the subscriber in execution of a decree
options.B: Can be attached to the extent of one-half in execution of a decree of a court
options.C: Is payable to the creditors of the subscriber on his retirement
options.D: Is not liable to attachment under any decree or order of a court

e: Under the Provident Fund rules applicable to railway servants, the amount at the credit of a subscriber in the GPF is not liable to attachment under any decree or order of a court.

q: A casual labourer on the Railways who has been granted temporary status becomes entitled to:

options.A: No benefit of any kind until he is absorbed in a regular post
options.B: Benefits only after he completes ten years of service with temporary status
options.C: The benefits admissible to temporary railway servants, such as leave and passes, in accordance with the rules
options.D: All the benefits of a confirmed railway servant, including pension for the entire period of his casual service

e: A casual labourer granted temporary status becomes entitled to the benefits admissible to temporary railway servants, such as leave and passes, under IREM; full pensionary benefits of a confirmed servant do not follow automatically.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 6 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 40,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twelve times his emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity slab for 5 to 11 years of qualifying service is 12 times emoluments: 6 years falls in this slab, so 12 x Rs 40,000 = Rs 4,80,000.

q: A condition of service of a railway servant is that he is liable to:

options.A: Serve only in the division in which he is initially posted
options.B: Be transferred, and to serve, anywhere on the Indian Railways
options.C: Decline a transfer to a station outside his zonal Railway
options.D: Serve only in the department in which he is initially appointed

e: A condition of service of a railway servant under IREM is that he is liable to be transferred to, and to serve, anywhere on the Indian Railways, not only in his initial division or department.

q: On the transfer of a railway servant in public interest, the members of his family do not travel along with him but perform the journey to the new station separately, within the prescribed time limits. In regard to travelling allowance for the journey of the family, the correct position is that it is:

options.A: Not admissible, as the family did not travel with the railway servant
options.B: Admissible only at half the normal rates
options.C: Admissible only where the family performs the journey by road
options.D: Admissible, as the members of the family are not required to travel along with the railway servant himself

e: Travelling allowance on transfer is admissible for family members even when they travel separately to the new station within the prescribed time limits; the TA rules do not require them to travel along with the railway servant.

q: A penalty imposed on a railway servant by an authority which is not competent to impose that penalty under the schedule of disciplinary powers is:

options.A: Valid, if the railway servant does not object to it
options.B: Valid, if it is not challenged within one year
options.C: Not valid, as a penalty can be imposed only by the authority competent to impose it under the schedule
options.D: Valid, if it is subsequently approved by the recognised trade union

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules and the schedule of disciplinary powers, a penalty imposed by an authority not competent to impose it is not valid; later approval or absence of objection does not cure the defect.

q: Where two cadres on the Railways are merged into a single cadre, the inter-se seniority of the staff in the merged cadre is ordinarily determined with reference to:

options.A: The length of continuous regular service rendered by them in the equivalent grade
options.B: Their dates of birth
options.C: Their educational qualifications
options.D: A fresh competitive examination held after the merger

e: On merger of cadres, inter-se seniority in the merged cadre is ordinarily determined with reference to the length of continuous regular service in the equivalent grade, as per the seniority rules in IREM.

q: The Composite Transfer Grant on retirement admissible to a railway servant who retires and settles down in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is:

options.A: 80 per cent of his last drawn basic pay
options.B: 100 per cent of his last drawn basic pay
options.C: 50 per cent of his last drawn basic pay
options.D: 33 per cent of his last drawn basic pay

e: Composite Transfer Grant on retirement is 100 percent of last basic pay where the retiree settles in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (or Lakshadweep), against the normal 80 percent elsewhere, under the 7th CPC orders.

q: A railway servant who is appointed or promoted to a post in a medical category connected with the safety of train running is required to:

options.A: Undergo a medical examination only at the time of his retirement
options.B: Produce a certificate of fitness from a private medical practitioner
options.C: Undergo no medical examination, as he was examined at the time of his initial appointment
options.D: Pass the prescribed medical examination for that category before he assumes the duties of the post

e: A railway servant appointed or promoted to a post in a medical category connected with safety of train running must pass the prescribed medical examination for that category before assuming the duties of the post, under IREM.

q: Special Casual Leave on the Railways is admissible, subject to the prescribed conditions and limits, to:

options.A: Any railway servant for attending to his private business
options.B: A railway servant for attending a marriage in his family
options.C: Representatives and office bearers of recognised trade unions, for attending union meetings and conferences
options.D: A railway servant for appearing in a court in connection with his private case

e: Special Casual Leave is admissible, subject to prescribed conditions and limits, to representatives and office bearers of recognised trade unions for attending union meetings and conferences, under IREM.

q: The service history of a gazetted railway servant, corresponding to the Service Book maintained for a non-gazetted railway servant, is maintained by:

options.A: The Accounts Office
options.B: The recognised trade union of the cadre
options.C: The Railway Recruitment Board
options.D: The gazetted railway servant himself

e: For gazetted railway servants, the service history corresponding to a non-gazetted servant's Service Book is maintained by the Accounts Office in the form of a History of Service.

q: Where an applicant under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is sensorily disabled and is unable to make a request for information in writing, the Central Public Information Officer shall:

options.A: Reject the application of the applicant
options.B: Render reasonable assistance to the applicant, including reducing his oral request to writing
options.C: Direct the applicant to approach a court for the information
options.D: Provide the information only through a legal practitioner engaged by the applicant

e: Under Section 6 of the RTI Act, where an applicant is sensorily disabled and cannot make a written request, the CPIO shall render reasonable assistance, including reducing the oral request to writing.

q: For confirmation in the post of Junior Accounts Assistant in the Accounts Department of the Railways, a directly recruited incumbent is required to:

options.A: Pass a trade test prescribed for artisan staff
options.B: Complete ten years of service in the post
options.C: Obtain a graduate degree from a recognised university
options.D: Pass the prescribed Appendix II departmental examination

e: Confirmation as Junior Accounts Assistant requires passing the prescribed Appendix II departmental examination of the Accounts Department, as per IREM.

q: 'Information', as defined in the Right to Information Act, 2005, includes information relating to a private body which:

options.A: Can never be disclosed to any applicant
options.B: Is held only outside India
options.C: Can be accessed by a public authority under any other law for the time being in force
options.D: Has been published in a newspaper or a journal

e: Under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, information includes information relating to a private body which can be accessed by a public authority under any other law for the time being in force.

q: In direct recruitment on the Railways, the relaxation in the upper age limit admissible to an ex-serviceman is ordinarily equal to:

options.A: Five years in all cases
options.B: The period of military service rendered by him, plus three years
options.C: Ten years in all cases
options.D: The period of military service rendered by him, without any addition

e: In direct recruitment, the upper age relaxation for an ex-serviceman is ordinarily the period of military service rendered by him plus three years, as per the recruitment rules in IREM.

q: When Dearness Allowance crosses 25%, the rates of House Rent Allowance in 'X', 'Y' and 'Z' class cities stand revised respectively to:

options.A: 24%, 16% and 8% of basic pay
options.B: 30%, 20% and 10% of basic pay
options.C: 27%, 18% and 9% of basic pay
options.D: 25%, 15% and 5% of basic pay

e: Under the 7th CPC HRA orders, when DA crosses 25 percent, HRA rates are revised from 24, 16 and 8 percent to 27, 18 and 9 percent of basic pay for X, Y and Z class cities respectively.

q: A Group 'C' railway servant who accepts a gift from a near relative or a personal friend having no official dealings with him, on an occasion such as a marriage or a religious function, is required to report the matter to the prescribed authority if the value of the gift exceeds:
e: A Group 'C' railway servant must report a gift from a near relative or personal friend if its value exceeds Rs 7,500. (Source: CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, Rule 13(2)(iii), as substituted by the CCS (Conduct) Amendment Rules, 2014, G.S.R. 149(E) dated 04.03.2014, DoPT.)

q: Information which would impede the process of investigation or apprehension or prosecution of offenders is exempt from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 under:

options.A: Section 8(1)(e)
options.B: Section 8(1)(d)
options.C: Section 8(1)(g)
options.D: Section 8(1)(h)

e: Information which would impede the process of investigation or apprehension or prosecution of offenders is exempt from disclosure under Section 8(1)(h) of the RTI Act.

q: Under Section 5(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, every public authority is required to:

options.A: Designate only one Central Public Information Officer, at its headquarters alone
options.B: Designate as many officers as Central Public Information Officers as may be necessary, in all administrative units or offices under its control, for providing information to persons requesting it
options.C: Designate Central Public Information Officers only in offices employing more than one hundred persons
options.D: Obtain the approval of the Central Information Commission for every officer designated by it

e: Section 5(1) of the RTI Act requires every public authority to designate as many CPIOs as may be necessary in all administrative units or offices under it to provide information to requesters.

q: 'Third party', as defined in the Right to Information Act, 2005, means:

options.A: Only a private company or firm
options.B: A person other than the citizen making a request for information, and includes a public authority
options.C: Only a citizen of a foreign country
options.D: The First Appellate Authority of the public authority

e: Under Section 2(n) of the RTI Act, third party means a person other than the citizen making the request for information, and includes a public authority.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the organisations specified in the Second Schedule to the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. The Act does not apply to the intelligence and security organisations specified in the Second Schedule to the Act.
2. The exclusion of such organisations does not extend to information pertaining to allegations of corruption and human rights violations.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Section 24 of the RTI Act excludes the intelligence and security organisations in the Second Schedule, but the exclusion does not apply to information on allegations of corruption and human rights violations.

q: A complaint of sexual harassment of a woman employee at the workplace is required to be made to the Internal Complaints Committee, under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, within a period of:

options.A: One month from the date of the incident
options.B: One year from the date of the incident
options.C: Five years from the date of the incident
options.D: Three months from the date of the incident, or from the date of the last incident in case of a series of incidents

e: Under Section 9 of the POSH Act, 2013, a complaint of sexual harassment must be made to the Internal Complaints Committee within three months of the incident, or of the last incident in a series.

q: An application by a railway servant to the Central Administrative Tribunal in a service matter is ordinarily required to be made within a period of:

options.A: One year from the date of the final order, or from the date on which the cause of action first accrued
options.B: Six months from the date of the final order
options.C: Two years from the date of the final order
options.D: Three years from the date of the final order

e: Under Section 21 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, a service-matter application to CAT must ordinarily be made within one year from the date of the final order or accrual of the cause of action.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the 'occupier' of a factory means:

options.A: The senior-most worker employed in the factory
options.B: The Inspector of Factories of the area
options.C: The person who has ultimate control over the affairs of the factory
options.D: The contractor who supplies labour to the factory

e: Under Section 2(n) of the Factories Act, 1948, the occupier of a factory is the person who has ultimate control over the affairs of the factory.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker in a railway workshop is allowed leave with wages for a period of four days or more, the wages due to him for the period of the leave are required to be paid:

options.A: Before his leave begins
options.B: Only after he returns to duty from the leave
options.C: Along with his salary for the succeeding month
options.D: Only if he submits a written application after rejoining duty

e: Under Section 81 of the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker is allowed leave with wages for four days or more, the wages for the leave period must be paid before his leave begins.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the definition of 'wages' under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936:
1. 'Wages' does not include any gratuity payable to the employed person on the termination of his employment.
2. 'Wages' includes any remuneration payable under any award or settlement between the parties, or under an order of a court.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct under Section 2(h) of the Payment of Wages Act: wages includes remuneration under an award, settlement or court order, but does not include gratuity payable on termination of employment.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, no fine shall be imposed on an employed person unless:

options.A: The Railway Board has approved the imposition of the fine
options.B: The employed person admits the charge against him in writing
options.C: The fine is recovered from him in a single instalment
options.D: He has been given an opportunity of showing cause against the fine proposed to be imposed

e: Under Section 8 of the Payment of Wages Act, no fine can be imposed on an employed person unless he has been given an opportunity of showing cause against the fine proposed.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a temporary (refundable) advance from a final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the General Provident Fund of a railway servant?

options.A: A temporary advance is refundable and is recovered from the subscriber in monthly instalments, whereas a final withdrawal is non-refundable and is not recovered from the subscriber
options.B: A temporary advance is non-refundable, whereas a final withdrawal is recovered from the subscriber in monthly instalments
options.C: A temporary advance is admissible only after the retirement of the subscriber, whereas a final withdrawal is admissible only during his service
options.D: There is no distinction between a temporary advance and a final withdrawal

e: A temporary advance from GPF is refundable and recovered in monthly instalments, whereas a final withdrawal is non-refundable and is not recovered from the subscriber, under the Provident Fund rules in IREM.

q: A railway servant, whose annual increment falls due on 1st July, avails Extra Ordinary Leave, otherwise than on medical certificate, for a period of two months during the year preceding the increment. The effect on his increment is that:

options.A: It is drawn on 1st July itself, as a matter of course
options.B: Its drawal is postponed by the period of such leave, the increment being drawn only after he completes the prescribed qualifying service, excluding the period of that leave
options.C: It is forfeited permanently on account of the leave
options.D: It is drawn on 1st July, but the arrears for two months are not payable to him

e: Extra Ordinary Leave, otherwise than on medical certificate, does not count for increment, so drawal of an increment due on 1st July is postponed by the period of such leave until the prescribed qualifying service is completed.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding Extra Ordinary Leave and pension:
1. Extra Ordinary Leave granted to a railway servant on medical certificate counts as qualifying service for the purpose of pension.
2. Extra Ordinary Leave granted to a railway servant otherwise than on medical certificate counts as qualifying service for pension in all cases, without any exception.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: EOL on medical certificate counts as qualifying service for pension under the RS (Pension) Rules, while EOL otherwise than on medical certificate counts only in specified circumstances, not in all cases.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding foreign service of a railway servant:
1. Service rendered by a railway servant on foreign service counts for pension in his parent cadre where the prescribed pension contribution in respect of him has been duly paid.
2. A railway servant on foreign service receives his pay from the revenues of the Government or of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: foreign service counts for pension in the parent cadre where the prescribed pension contribution has been duly paid; on foreign service the pay is paid by the foreign employer, not from Government or Railway revenues.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding Dress Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation:
1. The erstwhile Uniform Allowance stands subsumed in the Dress Allowance.
2. The erstwhile Kit Maintenance Allowance also stands subsumed in the Dress Allowance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: under the 7th CPC Dress Allowance orders, the erstwhile Uniform Allowance and the Kit Maintenance Allowance both stand subsumed in the Dress Allowance.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the negotiating machinery available to railway employees:
1. The Permanent Negotiating Machinery functions on the Railways at the Railway Board, zonal and divisional levels, for negotiation between the Administration and the recognised federations of railway employees.
2. Matters of common interest concerning Central Government employees generally are dealt with at the national level by the Permanent Negotiating Machinery of the Railways itself.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Permanent Negotiating Machinery works at Railway Board, zonal and divisional levels with recognised federations; matters common to Central Government employees generally go to the JCM, not the railway PNM.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding a railway servant under suspension:
1. Dearness Allowance is admissible on the subsistence allowance payable to a railway servant under suspension.
2. Subsistence allowance payable to a railway servant under suspension is a penalty specified in the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: DA is admissible on subsistence allowance under the RS (Pension) and D and A framework, but subsistence allowance is not a penalty listed in the RS (D and A) Rules.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the date on which commutation of pension becomes absolute:
1. Where a railway servant applies for commutation of a portion of his pension before his retirement, the commutation becomes absolute on the date of his retirement.
2. Where a railway pensioner applies for commutation of a portion of his pension after his retirement, the commutation becomes absolute on the date on which his application is received by the Head of Office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: for a post-retirement applicant under the Commutation Rules, commutation becomes absolute on the date the application is received by the Head of Office; for a pre-retirement applicant it becomes absolute on the date following retirement, not on the date of retirement itself.

q: A railway servant who is medically decategorised is absorbed in an alternative post carrying a lower scale of pay than the post held by him. In regard to his pay on such absorption, the correct position is that:

options.A: His pay is fixed at the minimum of the scale of the lower post in all cases
options.B: He is granted no protection of pay of any kind
options.C: He is compulsorily retired from service on such absorption
options.D: The pay drawn by him in the former post is protected, the difference being allowed to him as personal pay, to be absorbed in his future increments

e: On absorption of a medically decategorised railway servant in a lower-pay alternative post, the pay drawn in the former post is protected and the difference is allowed as personal pay to be absorbed in future increments, under IREM.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, a subscriber who retires voluntarily from service after completing the prescribed qualifying service for such retirement becomes entitled to receive the assured payout:

options.A: From the date of his voluntary retirement itself
options.B: From the date on which he would have attained the age of superannuation, had he continued in service
options.C: Only as a lump sum amount, payable on the date of his voluntary retirement
options.D: Only after he attains the age of 60 years, even where his age of superannuation is different

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, a subscriber who voluntarily retires after the prescribed qualifying service gets the assured payout only from the date he would have attained superannuation, not from the date of voluntary retirement.

q: Under the General Departmental Competitive Examination scheme on the Railways, serving railway employees who fulfil the prescribed qualifications and conditions are permitted to compete for:

options.A: 10 per cent of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of the specified posts
options.B: 50 per cent of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of the specified posts
options.C: All the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of the specified posts
options.D: 25 per cent of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of the specified posts

e: Under the GDCE scheme, serving railway employees meeting the prescribed qualifications may compete for 25 percent of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of the specified posts, as per IREM.

q: The Appendix III departmental examination of the Accounts Department on the Railways is the qualifying examination prescribed for promotion to the posts of:

options.A: Junior Accounts Assistant
options.B: Senior Section Officer (Accounts), Senior Travelling Inspector of Accounts and Senior Inspector of Station Accounts
options.C: Accounts Clerk
options.D: Assistant Financial Adviser

e: The Appendix III departmental examination is the qualifying examination prescribed for promotion to Senior Section Officer (Accounts), Senior Travelling Inspector of Accounts and Senior Inspector of Station Accounts, under IREM.

q: 'SPARROW', as used on the Railways, is the online system through which:

options.A: Pension cases of railway pensioners are processed by the Accounts Office
options.B: Privilege passes and Privilege Ticket Orders are issued to railway servants
options.C: The Annual Performance Appraisal Reports of gazetted (Group 'A' and Group 'B') officers are recorded and processed online
options.D: The monthly salary bills of railway servants are prepared

e: SPARROW is the online system through which the APARs of gazetted Group A and Group B officers are recorded and processed online.

q: Under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the power of revision conferred on the competent revising authority can be exercised by it:

options.A: Of its own motion (suo motu), as well as on an application made to it in that behalf
options.B: Only on an appeal preferred by the charged railway servant
options.C: Only within a period of 45 days from the date of the order sought to be revised
options.D: Only by the Railway Board, in all cases

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules, the revising authority may exercise the power of revision of its own motion (suo motu) as well as on an application made by the railway servant.

q: A railway servant is said to 'officiate' in a post when he:

options.A: Is confirmed in that post against a permanent vacancy
options.B: Is posted to that post on deputation in a foreign country
options.C: Is granted the pay of that post purely as a personal measure
options.D: Performs the duties of a post on which another railway servant holds a lien, or of a vacant post, without being appointed to it substantively

e: A railway servant is said to officiate in a post when he performs its duties, being a post on which another servant holds a lien or a vacant post, without being appointed to it substantively, as defined in IREM.

q: A railway servant falls short of the minimum qualifying service required for pensionary benefits by a few months. The position under the Railway Services (Pension) Rules regarding condonation of the deficiency is that:

options.A: The deficiency may be condoned by the competent authority up to one year
options.B: The deficiency may be condoned by the competent authority up to six months
options.C: No condonation is permissible - a deficiency in qualifying service shall not be condoned
options.D: The deficiency may be condoned by the competent authority up to two years

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, a deficiency in qualifying service for pensionary benefits shall not be condoned; unlike some other services, no condonation up to six months or one year is permissible on the Railways.

q: An appeal under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, which is preferred after the expiry of the prescribed period of 45 days, may nevertheless be entertained by the appellate authority if it is satisfied that:

options.A: The appellant is a member of a recognised trade union
options.B: The appellant had good and sufficient reasons for not preferring the appeal within the prescribed period
options.C: The penalty imposed on the appellant is a major penalty
options.D: The disciplinary authority has recommended the entertainment of the appeal

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules, a time-barred appeal filed after 45 days may be entertained if the appellate authority is satisfied that the appellant had good and sufficient reasons for the delay.

q: Family pension admissible to a minor child of a deceased railway servant is payable:

options.A: Directly to the minor child himself
options.B: To the eldest major member of the family, in all cases
options.C: Only after the child attains the age of majority
options.D: Through the guardian of the minor child

e: Family pension payable to a minor child of a deceased railway servant is paid through the guardian of the minor child, under the RS (Pension) Rules, not directly to the child.

q: A railway servant who is permanently absorbed in a public sector undertaking or in an autonomous body is entitled, in respect of the Leave on Average Pay standing at his credit on the date of his absorption, to:

options.A: No encashment of leave of any kind
options.B: Cash equivalent of the leave at his credit, subject to a maximum of 150 days only
options.C: Cash equivalent of the leave at his credit, subject to a maximum of 300 days
options.D: Encashment of the leave only after he retires from the absorbing organisation

e: On permanent absorption in a PSU or autonomous body, cash equivalent of Leave on Average Pay at credit is payable subject to a maximum of 300 days, under the leave rules in IREM.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant who becomes insolvent is required to:

options.A: Resign from railway service forthwith
options.B: Forthwith report the fact of his insolvency to the Government
options.C: Merely inform his immediate superior officer orally about it
options.D: Take no action, as his private financial affairs do not concern the Administration

e: Under Rule 18 of the RS (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant who becomes insolvent or remains in habitual indebtedness must forthwith report the fact to the Government.

q: A railway servant to whom a copy of his Annual Performance Appraisal Report has been communicated may submit a representation against the entries and the grading in the report to the competent authority within a period of:

options.A: 45 days from the date of receipt of the report
options.B: 90 days from the date of receipt of the report
options.C: Six months from the date of receipt of the report
options.D: 15 days from the date of receipt of the report

e: A railway servant to whom his APAR has been communicated may represent against the entries and grading to the competent authority within 15 days of receipt, under the APAR instructions.

q: At the time of entry into railway service, the date of birth of a railway servant is recorded in his Service Book primarily on the basis of:

options.A: A horoscope produced by the railway servant
options.B: His matriculation (secondary school leaving) certificate, where such a certificate is available
options.C: His oral declaration regarding his age
options.D: The medical certificate of fitness issued at the time of his appointment

e: At entry into service, the date of birth is recorded in the Service Book primarily on the basis of the matriculation or secondary school leaving certificate where available, under IREM.

q: The currency (period of validity) of a panel (select list) formed on the Railways for promotion to a selection post is ordinarily:

options.A: Two years, or till the panel is exhausted, whichever is earlier
options.B: One year, or till the panel is exhausted, whichever is earlier
options.C: Five years from the date of its formation
options.D: Unlimited, till all the empanelled railway servants are promoted

e: The currency of a panel for a selection post is ordinarily two years or till the panel is exhausted, whichever is earlier, under the selection rules in IREM.

q: On the reversion of a railway servant from deputation to an ex-cadre post to a post in his parent cadre, his pay in the parent cadre post is fixed:

options.A: At the minimum of the pay level of the parent cadre post, in all cases
options.B: At the pay last drawn by him in the ex-cadre post, in all cases
options.C: With reference to the pay which he would have drawn in the parent cadre post had he not proceeded on deputation, that is, on a notional basis
options.D: Only after deducting the whole of the Deputation (Duty) Allowance drawn by him

e: On reversion from an ex-cadre deputation post, pay in the parent cadre is fixed with reference to the pay the servant would have drawn in the parent cadre had he not gone on deputation, that is, on a notional basis.

q: Retention of a railway quarter by a railway servant beyond the normal permissible period after his transfer in public interest may be permitted on the ground of the education of his children, ordinarily up to:

options.A: A period of five years from the date of his transfer
options.B: The date of his retirement from service
options.C: No retention on this ground is permissible in any circumstances
options.D: The end of the academic session of his children

e: Retention of a railway quarter beyond the normal period after transfer in public interest may be permitted on the ground of children's education ordinarily up to the end of the academic session, under the quarter allotment rules.

q: In regard to the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity payable to a retired railway servant, the correct position is that it is:

options.A: Attachable in full by any private creditor in execution of a decree of a court
options.B: Attachable to the extent of one-half in execution of a decree of a court
options.C: Not liable to attachment at the instance of a private creditor under any decree or order of a court
options.D: Payable directly to the creditors of the railway servant on his retirement

e: Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity is not liable to attachment at the instance of a private creditor under any decree or order of a court, under the RS (Pension) Rules.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 2 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 55,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at six times his emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity slab for 1 to 5 years of qualifying service is 6 times emoluments: 2 years falls in this slab, so 6 x Rs 55,000 = Rs 3,30,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 12 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 50,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of monthly emoluments per completed six-monthly period: 12 years = 24 periods, so 24 x (Rs 50,000 / 4) = 24 x Rs 12,500 = Rs 3,00,000.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 48,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account, at 14 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:
e: NPS Government contribution is 14 percent of basic pay plus DA: basic plus DA = Rs 48,000 + Rs 24,000 = Rs 72,000, and 14 percent of Rs 72,000 = Rs 10,080.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 160 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 40,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Cash equivalent of leave salary = (basic pay + DA) / 30 x LAP days = (Rs 40,000 + Rs 20,000) / 30 x 160 = Rs 2,000 x 160 = Rs 3,20,000.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 75,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate, at 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 22,500 per month
options.B: Rs 75,000 per month
options.C: Rs 18,750 per month
options.D: Rs 37,500 per month

e: Enhanced rate family pension under the RS (Pension) Rules is 50 percent of last basic pay: 50 percent of Rs 75,000 = Rs 37,500 per month.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 200 days of Leave on Average Pay and 100 days of Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 60,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The total cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, the shortfall in Leave on Average Pay being made good by encashment of Leave on Half Average Pay at the rate of leave salary admissible on such leave, will be:
e: LAP part: (Rs 60,000 + Rs 30,000) / 30 x 200 = Rs 6,00,000. LHAP part for the 100-day shortfall at half rate: Rs 1,500 per day x 100 = Rs 1,50,000. Total = Rs 7,50,000.

q: During the period of joining time availed of by a railway servant on transfer in public interest, which is treated as duty, he is entitled to draw:

options.A: The pay of the new post to which he has been transferred
options.B: Subsistence allowance at the prescribed rate
options.C: The pay which he was drawing in the old post immediately before he was relieved of its charge
options.D: No pay for the period of joining time

e: Joining time on transfer in public interest is treated as duty, and during it the railway servant draws the pay he was drawing in the old post immediately before relief, under the joining time rules in IREM.

q: Information, the disclosure of which has been expressly forbidden by any court of law or tribunal, or the disclosure of which may constitute contempt of court, is exempt from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 under:

options.A: Section 8(1)(a)
options.B: Section 8(1)(b)
options.C: Section 8(1)(d)
options.D: Section 8(1)(j)

e: Information whose disclosure has been expressly forbidden by a court or tribunal, or which may constitute contempt of court, is exempt under Section 8(1)(b) of the RTI Act.

q: Information received in confidence from a foreign Government is exempt from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 under:

options.A: Section 8(1)(e)
options.B: Section 8(1)(h)
options.C: Section 8(1)(f)
options.D: Section 8(1)(i)

e: Information received in confidence from a foreign Government is exempt from disclosure under Section 8(1)(f) of the RTI Act.

q: Information, the disclosure of which would endanger the life or physical safety of any person, or identify the source of information given in confidence for law enforcement or security purposes, is exempt from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 under:

options.A: Section 8(1)(g)
options.B: Section 8(1)(b)
options.C: Section 8(1)(c)
options.D: Section 8(1)(d)

e: Information whose disclosure would endanger life or physical safety of any person, or identify a confidential source for law enforcement or security purposes, is exempt under Section 8(1)(g) of the RTI Act.

q: In an appeal proceeding under the Right to Information Act, 2005, the onus to prove that a denial of a request for information was justified lies on:

options.A: The applicant who made the request
options.B: The First Appellate Authority
options.C: The Central Information Commission
options.D: The Central Public Information Officer who denied the request

e: Under Section 19(5) of the RTI Act, in any appeal proceeding the onus to prove that a denial of the request was justified lies on the CPIO who denied the request.

q: Where a Central Public Information Officer has, without any reasonable cause, refused to receive an application for information or has not furnished information within the prescribed time, the Central Information Commission may, in addition to imposing a penalty on him:

options.A: Order his dismissal from service directly
options.B: Recommend disciplinary action against him under the service rules applicable to him
options.C: Direct the public authority to dismiss the applicant's request
options.D: Impose a penalty on the applicant for pursuing the matter

e: Under Section 20(2) of the RTI Act, where the CIC finds a CPIO has without reasonable cause refused to receive an application or delayed information, it may recommend disciplinary action against him under the applicable service rules.

q: An officer whose assistance has been sought by a Central Public Information Officer for the proper discharge of his duties under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is, for the purpose of any contravention of the provisions of the Act:

options.A: Exempt from all responsibility, the responsibility resting on the Central Public Information Officer alone
options.B: Responsible only to his own controlling officer
options.C: Treated as a Central Public Information Officer
options.D: Treated as the First Appellate Authority

e: Under Section 5(5) of the RTI Act, an officer whose assistance is sought by a CPIO is treated as a CPIO for the purpose of any contravention of the Act.

q: While inquiring into a complaint under the Right to Information Act, 2005, the Central Information Commission has, in respect of matters such as summoning and enforcing the attendance of persons and compelling them to give oral or written evidence on oath, the same powers as are vested in:

options.A: A civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure
options.B: A criminal court while trying an offence
options.C: The Central Administrative Tribunal
options.D: A departmental Inquiring Authority

e: Under Section 18(3) of the RTI Act, the CIC has, while inquiring into a complaint, the same powers as a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure in matters like summoning persons and compelling evidence on oath.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, an 'adolescent' means a person who:

options.A: Has completed his fourteenth year of age but has not completed his sixteenth year
options.B: Has completed his twelfth year of age but has not completed his fifteenth year
options.C: Has completed his sixteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year
options.D: Has completed his fifteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year

e: Under Section 2(c) of the Factories Act, 1948, an adolescent is a person who has completed his fifteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, no child worker shall be required or allowed to work in any factory for more than:

options.A: Six hours in any day
options.B: Four and a half hours in any day
options.C: Five hours in any day
options.D: Three hours in any day

e: Under Section 71 of the Factories Act, 1948, no child worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory for more than four and a half hours in any day.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a young person shall not be required or allowed to work on or near a dangerous machine in a factory unless:

options.A: He has completed five years of service in the factory
options.B: He is a member of a recognised trade union
options.C: He has been fully instructed as to the dangers connected with the machine and the precautions to be observed, and has received sufficient training in work on the machine or is under the adequate supervision of a person having thorough knowledge and experience of the machine
options.D: He has attained the age of twenty-one years

e: Under Section 27 of the Factories Act, a young person may work on a dangerous machine only if fully instructed about the dangers and precautions and sufficiently trained, or under adequate supervision of a person with thorough knowledge and experience of the machine.

q: Where an accident takes place in a factory governed by the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to railway workshops, and causes the death of a worker, the manager of the factory is required to:

options.A: Send notice of the accident to the Inspector of Factories and the other prescribed authorities
options.B: Merely record the accident in the muster roll of the factory
options.C: Report the accident only to the recognised trade union of the factory
options.D: Take no action, as the matter concerns only the family of the deceased worker

e: Under the Factories Act, where a factory accident causes death, the manager must send notice of the accident to the Inspector of Factories and the other prescribed authorities.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a young person shall not be required or allowed to work in any factory unless:

options.A: He has completed the prescribed course of training in a railway training school
options.B: He has been granted a privilege pass by the Administration
options.C: He has attained the age of sixteen years in all cases
options.D: A certificate of fitness for such work, granted to him by a certifying surgeon, is in the custody of the manager of the factory

e: Section 67 read with Section 68 of the Factories Act, 1948 bars a young person from working unless a certifying surgeon's certificate of fitness is in the manager's custody and he carries a token referring to it.

q: Which of the following deductions from the wages of an employed person is an authorised deduction under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936?

options.A: A deduction on account of a private loan taken by the employed person from a moneylender
options.B: A deduction towards a subscription to a political party collected by the employer
options.C: A deduction for payment of a fine imposed by a court on the employed person in a private dispute
options.D: A deduction for income-tax payable by the employed person

e: A deduction for income-tax payable by the employed person is an authorised deduction under Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.

q: A deduction from the wages of an employed person, towards payment of the premium on a life insurance policy of the employed person, can be made under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 only where:

options.A: The employer considers such a deduction to be convenient
options.B: The recognised trade union of the employed person demands it
options.C: The employed person has given his written authorisation for making such a deduction
options.D: The Accounts Officer of the establishment orders it

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, a deduction towards life insurance premium can be made only where the employed person has given written authorisation for the deduction.

q: Under Rule 10 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to evidence before a committee or any other authority, a railway servant shall not, except with the previous sanction of the Government:

options.A: Give evidence in connection with an inquiry conducted by any person, committee or authority
options.B: Submit a representation to his superior officer regarding his service matters
options.C: Appear as a witness in a departmental inquiry held against himself
options.D: Produce official records before his own disciplinary authority

e: Under Rule 10 of the RS (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not, except with the previous sanction of the Government, give evidence in connection with an inquiry conducted by any person, committee or authority.

q: Where an order of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement of a railway servant is set aside by a court of law, and the disciplinary authority decides to hold a further inquiry against him on the same allegations, the railway servant is deemed to have been placed under suspension by the appointing authority:

options.A: Only from the date on which the further inquiry is actually commenced
options.B: From the date of the judgment of the court setting aside the penalty
options.C: From the date on which he reports for duty after the judgment
options.D: From the date of the original order of dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules, where a dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement order is set aside by a court and further inquiry is decided upon, the servant is deemed suspended from the date of the original penalty order.

q: The report of the Inquiring Authority in a major penalty proceeding under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is required to contain:

options.A: Only the penalty which, in the opinion of the Inquiring Authority, should be imposed on the charged railway servant
options.B: The findings of the Inquiring Authority on each article of charge, together with the reasons therefor
options.C: A recommendation regarding the posting of the charged railway servant after the inquiry
options.D: The views of the recognised trade union on the charges against the railway servant

e: Under the RS (D and A) Rules, the Inquiring Authority's report must contain its findings on each article of charge together with the reasons for those findings; it does not recommend the penalty.

q: The power to make rules regulating the recruitment of persons to civil services and posts, and the conditions of service of persons appointed to such services and posts, until provision is made by an Act of the appropriate Legislature, is conferred on the President or the Governor, as the case may be, by the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 310
options.B: Article 311
options.C: Article 309
options.D: Article 312

e: Article 309 of the Constitution empowers the President or the Governor, as the case may be, to make rules regulating recruitment and conditions of service of civil servants until the appropriate Legislature makes an Act.

q: Under the Constitution, a person who is a member of a civil service of the Union, or who holds a civil post under the Union, holds office:

options.A: During the pleasure of the President
options.B: Till he attains the age of superannuation in all circumstances
options.C: Only during the pleasure of the Minister in charge of his department
options.D: For a fixed tenure of five years at a time

e: Under Article 310 of the Constitution, a member of a civil service of the Union or holder of a civil post under the Union holds office during the pleasure of the President.

q: Article 311(2) of the Constitution provides that a person who is a member of a civil service of the Union, or who holds a civil post under the Union, shall not be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank except:

options.A: With the prior approval of the Union Public Service Commission in every case
options.B: After obtaining the orders of the President of India in every case
options.C: By an order issued in the name of the Minister in charge
options.D: After an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges against him and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those charges

e: Article 311(2) provides that no civil servant shall be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank except after an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard on them.

q: 'Retiring pension', as a class of pension under the pension rules applicable to railway servants, is granted to a railway servant who:

options.A: Retires on attaining the age of superannuation in the normal course
options.B: Is retired from service in accordance with the rules before attaining the age of superannuation, otherwise than on invalidation or on abolition of his post
options.C: Is discharged from service on account of misconduct
options.D: Resigns from service of his own accord before retirement

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, retiring pension is granted to a railway servant retired before attaining superannuation in accordance with the rules, otherwise than on invalidation or abolition of post.

q: Where a railway pensioner dies leaving arrears of pension unpaid, and no nomination made by him for receiving the arrears of pension subsists, the arrears are payable to:

options.A: The pension disbursing bank, which retains the amount
options.B: The Staff Benefit Fund of the Railway
options.C: The legal heirs of the deceased pensioner
options.D: No one, as the arrears lapse to the Government in every such case

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, where a pensioner dies leaving unpaid arrears of pension and no subsisting nomination, the arrears are payable to his legal heirs.

q: 'Record', as defined in the Right to Information Act, 2005, includes:

options.A: Any document, manuscript and file, any microfilm, microfiche and facsimile copy of a document, any reproduction of an image embodied in such microfilm, and any other material produced by a computer or any other device
options.B: Only printed files maintained in the record room of the public authority
options.C: Only documents which have been published in the Official Gazette
options.D: Only material held in electronic form by the public authority

e: Under Section 2(i) of the RTI Act, record includes any document, manuscript and file, microfilm, microfiche and facsimile copies, reproductions of images in such microfilm, and any other material produced by a computer or other device.

q: In regard to Leave Travel Concession, the correct position regarding the family members of a railway servant is that:

options.A: The family members must invariably travel along with the railway servant himself
options.B: The family members can avail the concession only after the railway servant has himself availed it
options.C: The family members can avail the concession only in the same block in which the railway servant retires
options.D: The family members may avail the Leave Travel Concession independently of the railway servant, and need not travel along with him

e: Under the LTC rules, family members may avail the Leave Travel Concession independently of the railway servant and need not travel along with him.

q: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, the erstwhile Bad Climate Allowance admissible to railway servants stands:

options.A: Doubled for servants posted in areas with a difficult climate
options.B: Subsumed in the Tough Location Allowance
options.C: Merged with the House Rent Allowance
options.D: Continued separately at the pre-revised rates

e: Under the 7th CPC allowance rationalisation, the erstwhile Bad Climate Allowance stands subsumed in the Tough Location Allowance and is not continued separately.
